purposes:
- response: Develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset while ensuring the
    methods promote privacy, accountability, and clinical benefit, and while promoting a new
    generation of AI clinicians and scientists — stated in the NIH RePORTER abstract as the
    project's overarching goal.
- response: Work with projects to create ethically sourced datasets and tools around Artificial
    Intelligence and to create best practices for AI in health — stated as the goal of the
    CHoRUS project on the project website.
- response: Develop the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready data set
    to answer the grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness — stated as the
    goal of the CHoRUS Network in the GitHub organization overview (captured 2025-11-14).
tasks:
- response: Characterizing acute and critical care illness, named in the NIH RePORTER abstract
    as an aim of the ML/AI applications the project will generate data for.
- response: Predicting complications, named in the NIH RePORTER abstract as an aim of the
    ML/AI applications the project will generate data for.
- response: Measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness, named
    in the NIH RePORTER abstract as an aim of the ML/AI applications the project will generate
    data for.
addressing_gaps:
- response: The NIH RePORTER abstract states that there is an urgent need for infrastructure
    to support artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) in critical care, and
    that developing high-resolution multi-center data sets is a critical first step towards
    actionable and trustworthy AI.

sampling_strategies:

    legal framework for collecting data at scale, sampling to ensure comprehensive sets of
    patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies.
- strategies: Planned. The GitHub organization overview (captured 2025-11-14) states that
    federated access will enable sampling methods to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort.
preprocessing_strategies:
- preprocessing_details: Standardization of structured electronic health record data to the
    OMOP common data model. The project website reports 1.6 Billion rows of EHR OMOP data
    in the current released dataset; the NIH RePORTER abstract describes standardizing data
    to the OMOP Common Data Model as a planned project activity.
- preprocessing_details: Clinical notes are extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit,
    per the dataset table in the cohort 2 informational webinar.
- preprocessing_details: Planned. The NIH RePORTER abstract states that the project will transform
    data using approaches that limit re-identification.
labeling_strategies:
- labeling_details: Planned. The NIH RePORTER abstract states that the project will develop
    capabilities across a multi-center network to acquire, standardize, tokenize, store, visualize,
    and label data; the GitHub organization overview (captured 2025-11-14) states that a visualization
    and annotation environment will label data with targets important for prediction.

  usage_notes: Stated in the NIH RePORTER project narrative as the purpose for which the CHoRUS

description: CHoRUS is the multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution critical care dataset
  generated by the CHoRUS data generation project, which the project website describes as
  one data generation project of four in the National Institute of Health (NIH) funded Bridge2AI
  consortium. The cohort 2 informational webinar (September 9, 2025) presents the dataset
  as multicenter, multimodal and high-resolution, built from retrospective data collection
  and controlled access; as of August 2025 it covers 14 different hospitals with over 45K
  unique admissions. That webinar states that OMOP and telemetry data are in an enclave, except
  that clinical notes are stored locally apart from tokens, that 1000 images are currently
  available with de-identification in process for a larger cohort, and that EEG extraction
  is in process at this point. The data types it lists are demographics, medication administration,
  procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses, clinical notes, imaging, waveform telemetry and
  waveform EEG. The project website's Current Released Dataset snapshot reports 50,000 patient
  admissions from ICU, PICU, and NICU, 1.6 Billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions
  with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data; the website describes the project as the
  collection of multi-modal data across 14 different hospitals, with 60+ CHoRUS consortium
  members across 20 different institutions, while the GitHub organization overview (captured
  2025-11-14) states that the collaboration spans 20 academic centers, of which 14 will contribute
  as Data Acquisition centers. Alongside the data pillar, the website states that the CHoRUS
  consortium evaluates community perspectives on clinical care AI to find ways to increase
  trustworthiness of provenance and privacy in AI, and that the project is dedicated to training
  engineers, data scientists, and clinicians.
notes: 'The NIH RePORTER record for the supporting award (application ID 10472824) titles
  the project "Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards
  (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI", with a project start of 2022-09-01 and a project end of 2026-11-30.
  The cohort 2 informational webinar lists a Bridge2AI CHoRUS Leadership Team of Eric Rosenthal
  (Massachusetts General Hospital), Azra Bihorac (University of Florida), Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth
  Houston), Yulia Strekalova (University of Florida), Parisa Rashidi (University of Florida)
  and Manlik Kwong (Tufts University). The project website lists Ciera McCrary, MGH, Program
  Manager (cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu) under Contact Us, and carries the banner "This repoitory
  is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives."'
source_caveats: 'Admission counts come from two sources with different observation times and
  are compatible rather than contradictory: the project website (documentation, tier 2) reports
  50,000 patient admissions in its Current Released Dataset snapshot, while the cohort 2 informational
  webinar (tutorial, tier 4) reports over 45K unique admissions as of August 2025. The webinar''s
  dataset table is extracted from the PDF with its columns and rows interleaved, so only pairings
  that appear adjacently in the extracted text are recorded here (demographics with OMOP;
  clinical notes with OHNLP; imaging with DICOM; waveform telemetry with WFDB; waveform EEG
  with EDF+ and Persyst); the per-row access control and metadata cells cannot be reliably
  attributed to individual data types, although the slide''s prose states controlled access.

  in its repository README, which concerns the chorus-ai repositories; it is therefore not
  recorded as a license for the dataset. The webinar''s leadership slide names individuals
  without stating their role with respect to the dataset, so those names are carried in notes

  spells it, "cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu".'
